slides.title: Delivering Engineering Software Solutions

slides.takeaway: When workflow rules are encoded into systems, risk drops and efficiency scales.

notes.intent: Establish positioning as a strategic, cross-department systems builder. Open with a personal positioning statement: who you are, why you built these tools, and why this matters to the people in the room.
notes.summary: Introduce the talk as a cross-functional, systems-driven approach to reducing manual friction and operational risk. Lead with the anchor stat to immediately ground the audience in tangible outcomes.

content.heading: FROM WORKFLOW FRICTION TO VALIDATED SYSTEMS
content.tagline: Cross-functional engineering workflows translated into reliable, scalable software platforms.
content.statLabel: hours of manual engineering work eliminated annually

slides.title: Where Risk Enters the Workflow
slides.subtitle: When system logic is fragmented, friction appears at every stage of design and delivery.
slides.takeaway: When validation happens late, friction multiplies across the workflow.

notes.intent: This is the buy-in moment. If the audience doesn't feel this pain, nothing after it lands. Slow down here. Pick ONE bullet per stage and tell a micro-story. Ask the audience: 'How many of you have caught something at Quoting that should have been caught at Design?'
notes.summary: Show where risk enters the engineering workflow when complex systems are designed using fragmented logic. Every bullet should feel like 'that's my Tuesday' to an engineer in the room.

stages.title: DESIGN
bullets: Cross-referencing Vortex media constraints across 3+ spreadsheets
Design quality varies by engineer experience level

stages.title: VALIDATION
bullets: Compliance mismatches caught after calculation, not before
Cross-zone rule conflicts discovered at review stage
Rework triggered by late-stage rule discovery

stages.title: QUOTING
bullets: Partcode + pricing reconciliation requires engineering confirmation
Sales waiting on engineering for basic compatibility answers

stages.title: DELIVERY
bullets: Audit findings trace back to manual entry variance
No standardized output template across teams

content.caption: "Fragmented logic shifts validation downstream and multiplies risk."

slides.title: Powerful Products. Complex Systems.
slides.subtitle: Engineering excellence introduces configuration complexity.
slides.takeaway: As product capability increases, structured tooling becomes necessary to reduce risk and variability.

notes.intent: Bridge from abstract friction to concrete products. Pick Vortex as the lead: 'This is one of the most capable things we make. And it's one of the hardest to configure correctly.' Then gesture to VicFlex: 'VicFlex is a different kind of complexity — high frequency, high variability. I'll come back to that.'
notes.summary: Increased product capability naturally results in system-level configuration density. These aren't hypothetical — these are the systems I've built tools for.

slides.title: Encoding Engineering Judgment
slides.subtitle: From manual variance to rule-based validation
slides.takeaway: When requirements become code, outputs become consistent — and risk shifts upstream.

notes.intent: Prove that automation here means structural risk reduction, not just calculation speed. Narrate the transformation: point left ('This is what it looked like before — four disconnected inputs'), center ('This is the rules engine I built'), right ('Same result, every time'). Then land the takeaway line verbatim.
notes.summary: Demonstrates the transition from spreadsheet-based logic to an encoded rules engine with real-time validation and standardized outputs. This is the Vortex v1 story.

afterItems: Validation at the point of entry

slides.title: From Tool to Platform
slides.subtitle: Project-Level Orchestration
slides.takeaway: Project-level hierarchy turns many enclosures into one consistent BOM and documentation set.

notes.intent: This is the 'zoom out' moment. Bridge from v1: 'Everything I just showed you — the configurator — solves one system at a time. But real projects don't have one system. They have dozens of enclosures across multiple zones.' Walk through the before animation, then the after. Land it: 'This is the difference between a tool and a platform.'
notes.summary: Shows how enclosure → zone → system → project aggregation enables cross-zone validation and standardized outputs. This is the Vortex v2 story — the natural escalation from single-system to project-wide.

slides.title: Small Automation, Big Leverage
slides.subtitle: Same thinking. Smaller scale. Bigger aggregate impact.
slides.takeaway: Automating the decisions made 40 times creates more impact than optimizing the ones made once.

notes.intent: Deliberate change of pace after the Vortex arc. Tell the human story: 'I watched an engineer do this 40 times in a single project. Each time — open a PDF, find the right table, cross-reference the bracket, type the result. Three minutes each. That's two hours per project just on bracket compatibility.' Then: 'I wrote a filter that does it instantly. Sounds trivial. But automating the decision you make 40 times creates more impact than optimizing the one you make once.'
notes.summary: Illustrates how targeted automation of a high-frequency lookup eliminated engineering gatekeeping and accelerated quoting. Proves the approach scales down to small, targeted wins — not just big platforms.

content.problemDescription: Engineers repeatedly filtered bracket compatibility across PDF matrices and product reference documents — 40+ times per project, every project.

slides.title: How I Build Internal Platforms
slides.subtitle: A cross-functional lifecycle from concept to deployment.
slides.takeaway: Alignment + validation + iteration is what makes tools scalable.

notes.intent: Now that the audience has seen three case studies, this slide answers 'How do you actually do this?' Frame it: 'Every tool I just showed you followed this same lifecycle.' Don't try to cover all 6 phases — pick 2-3 and connect them to specific case studies. E.g., 'Discovery is where I validated that the Vortex friction was structural, not a training gap.'
notes.summary: Formal product lifecycle applied even for internal tools. Includes immersion with project engineers, prototyping with calc designers, and validation sprints with test groups. The methodology is now proven by the case studies that preceded it.

slides.title: The Automation Playbook
slides.subtitle: Principles that guide the work
slides.takeaway: The goal is to make the correct way the easy way.

notes.intent: Elevate from case studies to philosophy. Pick 3 principles and tie each back: 'Validate Early — that's the Configurator. Encode Rules — that's the bracket filter. Institutionalize — that's why the Builder exists.' Then land the callout: 'Every principle boils down to one idea: make the correct way the easy way.'
notes.summary: Synthesize lessons from all case studies into a repeatable, transferable approach. These aren't abstractions — they're extracted from real projects.

tiles.title: Validate Early
tiles.description: Stop errors at the point of entry — not three stages downstream.

tiles.title: Encode Rules
tiles.description: Turn the 200-page manual into code that enforces compliance.

tiles.title: Cut Handoffs
tiles.description: One data entry from sales to build. No re-keying, no reconciliation.

tiles.title: Standardize
tiles.description: Same output format, every project, every engineer, every time.

tiles.title: Institutionalize
tiles.description: Knowledge lives in code, not in the heads of senior engineers.

tiles.title: High Coherence
tiles.description: Pricing and configuration always match. No post-hoc reconciliation.

content.callout: The goal is to make the correct way the easy way.

slides.title: Impact You Can Measure
slides.subtitle: Reliability, Speed, & Consistency
slides.takeaway: Automation isn't about flash — it's about workflow reliability.

notes.intent: Lead with the strongest metric: '400 hours. That's how much manual engineering work we've eliminated annually. Here's the math: 10 engineers, 2 hours a week, across 20 weeks.' Then: '80% fewer logic regressions — measured before and after configurator launch.' And: '100% output consistency — structurally impossible to produce a non-standard output.'
notes.summary: Every metric has a defensible basis. No soft qualifiers. Engineers respect numbers but detect soft ones — these are grounded.

slides.title: What Should We Automate Next?
slides.subtitle: The real portfolio — what's live, what's building, and where we need input.
slides.takeaway: If a workflow is repetitive and rule-based, it's a candidate for code.

notes.intent: Shift from presenter to collaborator. 'This is my actual backlog. These are real projects, not hypotheticals.' Point to each column. End with the explicit ask: 'If any of these resonate — or if you have a workflow that's not on this board — come find me after. I'm looking for the next problem to solve.'
notes.summary: Showcase the real project pipeline to invite collaboration and surface new opportunities. Every item on this board is a real project in development or discovery.
